title: Series: The Real Story of Troy (EN)

beats.say: Everyone thought it was a legend. But Troy is real, and it's in *Türkiye*.
Almost 3,000 years ago, Homer told the story of the Trojan War in the *Iliad*.
For centuries, people believed the city was just a *myth*.
Until archaeologists started digging at *Hisarlık Hill*.
Under the hill they found not one city, but *nine cities* stacked on top of each other.
Those layers cover roughly *4,000 years* of history.
Massive walls, towers and *city gates* are still standing today.
In 1998, Troy became a *UNESCO World Heritage* Site.
In Part 2: the man who found Troy, and his *explosive* methods.
*Follow* so you don't miss it.

beats.say: The man who found Troy *destroyed* part of it while he was digging.
German businessman *Heinrich Schliemann* began digging at Hisarlık in 1870.
But the real clue came from an Englishman, *Frank Calvert*.
Calvert *owned* part of the hill and was sure it was Troy.
Schliemann wanted Homer's Troy, so he cut a giant *trench* through the hill.
Reportedly, he even used *dynamite*.
He *wrecked* the cities lying above the layer he was looking for.
Today, visitors can still see the huge *Schliemann trench*.
In Part 3: the *gold treasure* found in 1873.
*Follow* so you don't miss it.

beats.say: The gold treasure of Troy isn't in Türkiye today. It's in *Moscow*.
In 1873, Schliemann saw *gold* shining in the dirt.
Diadems, earrings, necklaces and thousands of *gold pieces*.
He named it *Priam's Treasure*, after the king of Troy in Homer.
His wife Sophia posed for a *photo* wearing the jewels.
But the treasure was *smuggled* out of the Ottoman Empire.
It went to Berlin. Then in 1945, at the end of the war, it *vanished*.
In 1993 the truth came out: it was in Moscow's *Pushkin Museum*.
Should it go back to Türkiye? *Comment below*.

beats.say: The famous Trojan Horse never appears in Homer's *Iliad*.
The Iliad ends *before* Troy falls.
The wooden horse gets only a short mention in the *Odyssey*.
The most detailed version comes from the Roman poet *Virgil*.
So what does history say? There's *no evidence* of a wooden horse.
Some historians think the horse stood for a *siege engine*.
Others think it describes an *earthquake* that broke the walls.
But we do know one layer of Troy was destroyed by *fire*.
In Part 5: where did the giant horse in Çanakkale *come from*?
*Follow* so you don't miss it.

beats.say: The giant Trojan Horse on Çanakkale's seafront is actually a *movie prop*.
It was used in the 2004 film *Troy* and then gifted to the city.
Today it's one of the most *photographed* spots in town.
The real history is a short drive away, at the *Troy Museum*.
The museum opened in 2018, which Türkiye declared the *Year of Troy*.
And Troy is back in the *spotlight*.
Christopher Nolan's *The Odyssey* brought the Troy story to millions again.
But the real stage of the legend is right here: *Hisarlık Hill*, Türkiye.
